spec.title: Verdict
spec.description: The same rules as the vulnerability alerts. Red when a critical alert fires: a loaded KEV CVE or a loaded critical in a workload that can be reached from outside the cluster. Amber for a warning: a loaded KEV CVE that is not exposed, a loaded critical with a fix, or a loaded CVE with an EPSS of 10% or more. Grey "Pending" when no alert fires yet but at least one is pending: its condition holds, and it fires after an hour (for: 1h) if that stays so, e.g. the first hour after a new finding or a fresh install. Green only when nothing fires or is pending. Grey "Data not current" when the exporter or the daily scan fails. Follows Namespace and Workload only: the alerts know no image, CVE or severity filter. Since yesterday: workloads whose alerts started (new) or all stopped (resolved) in the last 24 hours; hidden when nothing changed or the exporter has no data from a day ago. This counts workloads, not CVEs: an alert also starts when a CVE gets on the KEV list or above 10% EPSS, becomes loaded or the workload becomes exposed. Click a since yesterday count to see which CVEs changed on the Changes tab, any other count to open the Workloads tab with those workloads selected.

spec.title: Exposure status
spec.description: Can a loaded critical or KEV CVE be reached from outside the cluster? Red when VulnerabilityRelevantKEVExposed or VulnerabilityRelevantCriticalExposed fires, grey "Exposure pending" when one of them is pending (it fires after an hour if that stays so), green when neither; the Exposure tab has the entry points. Follows Namespace and Workload only, like the verdict.

spec.title: All clusters
spec.description: The verdict of every cluster, whatever Cluster is set to: the same colours and numbers as the Verdict banner of that cluster (workloads with a firing alert; pending: workloads whose alerts fire after an hour if nothing changes, when none fires yet). spec.expression: WITH a AS (SELECT cluster, alertname, alertstate AS st, severity, namespace, workload FROM PALC WHERE __value__ >= 0), ex AS (SELECT cluster FROM PCL WHERE __value__ >= 0), cl AS (SELECT cluster FROM ex UNION SELECT cluster FROM a), c AS ( SELECT cl.cluster, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.st = 'firing' AND a.alertname LIKE 'VulnerabilityRelevant%' AND a.severity IN ('critical', 'warning') THEN CONCAT(a.namespace, '/', a.workload) END) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.st = 'pending' AND a.alertname LIKE 'VulnerabilityRelevant%' AND a.severity IN ('critical', 'warning') THEN CONCAT(a.namespace, '/', a.workload) END) AS pn, MAX(CASE WHEN a.st = 'firing' AND a.alertname LIKE 'VulnerabilityRelevant%' AND a.severity = 'critical' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crit, MAX(CASE WHEN a.st = 'firing' AND a.alertname IN ('KubescapeCveExporterFailing', 'KubescapeDailyScanMissing') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS stale FROM cl LEFT JOIN a ON a.cluster = cl.cluster GROUP BY cl.cluster) SELECT c.cluster AS Cluster, CASE WHEN c.stale = 1 OR ex.cluster IS NULL THEN 'data not current' WHEN c.crit = 1 THEN CONCAT('', REPLACE(CONCAT('action needed: ', c.n), ' ', ' '), '') WHEN c.n > 0 THEN CONCAT('', REPLACE(CONCAT('attention: ', c.n), ' ', ' '), '') WHEN c.pn > 0 THEN CONCAT('', REPLACE(CONCAT('pending: ', c.pn), ' ', ' '), '') ELSE 'no action needed' END AS Verdict FROM c LEFT JOIN ex ON ex.cluster = c.cluster ORDER BY CASE WHEN c.stale = 1 OR ex.cluster IS NULL THEN 1 WHEN c.crit = 1 THEN 3 WHEN c.n > 0 THEN 2 WHEN c.pn > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END DESC, c.n DESC, c.cluster

spec.title: Funnel
spec.description: Unique critical and high CVEs, from everything in the running images to what is loaded, exploitable (on CISA's KEV list, or an EPSS of 10% or more) and exploitable in a workload that can be reached from outside the cluster. Each step is part of the one before. The bar is as wide as the step's share of the first: purple critical, red high. Click a step to list its CVEs (the list cannot be filtered to exploitable or exposed, it is sorted that way). The Exposure status card counts something else: workloads with any loaded critical or KEV CVE behind an entry point.

e AS (SELECT cve, __value__ AS epss FROM PE WHERE __value__ >= 0),
k AS (SELECT cve, MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(ransomware, '')) = 'known' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ransom FROM PK WHERE __value__ >= 0 GROUP BY cve)
, t AS (SELECT rv.cve, COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(rv.namespace, '/', rv.workload)) AS n,
    MAX(CASE rv.severity WHEN 'critical' THEN 3 WHEN 'high' THEN 2 WHEN 'medium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sevr, MAX(CASE WHEN k.cve IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS kev,
    MAX(COALESCE(e.epss, -1)) AS epss
  FROM rv LEFT JOIN k ON k.cve = rv.cve LEFT JOIN e ON e.cve = rv.cve
  WHERE rv.severity IN ('critical', 'high') GROUP BY rv.cve)

FROM t ORDER BY t.n DESC, t.kev DESC, t.epss DESC, t.sevr DESC, t.cve LIMIT 8

spec.title: To do today
spec.description: One row per workload container with a firing vulnerability alert: critical alerts first, then KEV, exposure, EPSS and a fixable critical. Follows Namespace and Workload only: the alerts know no image, CVE or severity filter. KEV: a loaded CVE is exploited in the wild. EPSS: the highest chance of exploitation in the next 30 days among its loaded CVEs. public / restricted / unknown: how it can be reached from outside; no chip: not exposed. fixable critical: a loaded critical has a fixed package version (the image itself may not have a release with it yet); critical without fix: one has none. CVEs: the worst CVE that triggered an alert (empty when the data no longer holds the alert's CVEs), then how many other loaded CVEs the container has: click the CVE for that CVE, click +N more for every CVE of the workload on the CVEs tab.

spec.title: Changes
spec.description: One row per loaded CVE that changed in a workload container, and per workload whose exposure changed. new: new image (the CVE came with another image), new workload, newly found. now loaded / no longer loaded: only the load status changed, in the same image (a restart makes a pod load more at start); listed after the other changes. Changed: on KEV or off KEV, EPSS ≥ 10% or below, now critical or no longer critical, fix available. Exposure rows list the loaded critical and KEV CVEs the change puts within (or out of) reach. Resolved: fixed (no longer in the image), workload gone. A workload is matched without a trailing revision hash (Crossplane providers); a container whose new image has no relevancy data yet shows nothing until it has. alert: the change can start or stop a vulnerability alert; those rows come first. Severity: now, or at the comparison moment for resolved rows. Click a workload or CVE to open it on its tab. With Show all and no namespace, workload, image or CVE selected, only CVEs loaded on one side are compared.

spec.title: Workloads
spec.description: One row per workload container with a CVE in its image, riskiest first: a loaded KEV CVE, an exposed loaded critical, loaded criticals, an EPSS of 10% or more, exposure, loaded highs. init: an init container, which runs briefly at start, so nothing of its image is loaded. KEV: loaded CVEs on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. EPSS: the highest chance of exploitation in the next 30 days among its loaded CVEs (a row holds several CVEs, so the highest one) (orange from 10%, the alert threshold; – when none has a score). spec.title: Upgrades
spec.description: Every package bump that clears CVEs in the images of the selected workloads (following Show: with Show relevant only bumps that clear a loaded CVE). Fix: the installed version and the lowest version that fixes all CVEs of that package version (a fixed package version does not mean the image has a release with it yet). Clears: the unique critical (purple), high (red) and medium (orange) CVEs the bump removes, loaded at runtime (solid) and all (tinted). KEV: loaded CVEs it clears that are on the KEV list. EPSS: the highest EPSS among the loaded CVEs it clears. Exposure: the most open way in to the workloads running the image. KEV first, then loaded criticals.

spec.title: By package
spec.description: The same bumps per package over all images of the selection (following Show), for a dependency or base image layer that many images share: one fix, many images. Fix: the package, the installed version (or how many versions) and the highest of the per-image fixed versions. Images and Workloads: where the package is installed with a fix available. Clears: the unique critical, high and medium CVEs, loaded (solid) and all (tinted). KEV: loaded CVEs on CISA's KEV list it clears. KEV first, then loaded criticals.

spec.expression: WITH x AS (SELECT namespace, workload, via, gateway, COALESCE(hostname, '') AS hostname, access FROM PX WHERE __value__ >= 0) SELECT CONCAT(namespace, '/', workload) AS Workload, namespace AS ns, workload AS wl, via AS Via, gateway AS Gateway, hostname AS Hostname, CASE CASE access WHEN 'public' THEN 3 WHEN 'restricted' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END WHEN 3 THEN 'public' WHEN 2 THEN 'restricted' WHEN 1 THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'internal' END AS Access FROM x ORDER BY CASE access WHEN 'public' THEN 3 WHEN 'restricted' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END DESC, namespace, workload, via, hostname

options.content: **Trends and data**: how fresh the data behind this dashboard is, and the CVEs of the selected workloads per day over the last 30 days, whatever the time picker says.

spec.title: Data health
spec.description: How old the data behind this dashboard is, red once the matching alert fires. EPSS (FIRST, daily) and KEV (CISA, a few times a week): when the publisher released the data the exporter has (KubescapeCveFeedDataOld). Exporter last list: KubescapeCveExporterFailing. Last daily scan: the kubevuln-scheduler CronJob (KubescapeDailyScanMissing). Feed downloads: the oldest successful feed download (KubescapeCveFeedStale). Images not scanned: running images without any Kubescape scan, which no other panel counts (no alert; the Images tab lists them).
